This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.10,00,000/ for the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 31082018 at about 6.00 p.m., the Petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider in a motor cycle bearing NO.TN37 B5429 which was ridden by one Mr.B.M.Siddesh.

According to him when the said bike reached near Balaji Granites,
Malur town, Kolar District, one tractor and trailer bearing No.KA40 T9699 &
KA03T1376 which was driven by its driver came from wrong side of the road in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against petitioner's motor cycle.
Due to the impact, the Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to Government hospital, Malur and thereafter he was shifted to R.L.Jalappa hospital, Kolar.
3. Prior to the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was working as water proof mechanic/mason in PVR building solutions and was earning Rs.20,000/ per month.
Due to the accident, he has sustained grievous injuries causing permanent disablement.

4. The Respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending tractor and trailer and therefore, Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
5. In pursuance of service of notice, the Respondent No.1 remained absent and was placed exparte.
Respondent No.2 appeared before the court through it's counsel and filed objections to the main petition.

In the Objection Statement of Respondent No.2, it denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving by the driver of tractor and trailer by its driver.
Further it has denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the accident and the expenses incurred for the medical treatment.
Further it admitted the issuance of policy in respect of tractor and trailer bearing Regn.No.KA40T9699 and KA03T1376 in favour of 1st respondent.
It is further contended that the accident was not caused due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by its driver.
Further contended that the accident occurred due to negligence of rider of motor cycle.
Further contended that the driver of tractor and trailer was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.

The respondent No.1 Jagannatha H.R vs M.Lakshman on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179668796/
2 knowing fully well entrusted the vehicle to a person who did not possess valid and effective driving licence to drive the same on the date of accident.
Thereby the owner of the tractor and trailer committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
It also contends that the vehicle bearing No.KA40T9699 and KA03T1376 was not at all involved in the alleged accident.
The said vehicle has been falsely implicated in this case for the purpose of claiming compensation from the insurance company.
Hence, among these and other grounds, Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
6. On the basis of the above pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues.
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in the nature of permanent disablement on 31082018 at about 6.00 p.m. near Balaji Granites, Malur town, Ko9lar district, in an accident arising due to rash and negligent driving of driver of tractor and trailer bearing No.KA 40T9699 & KA03T1376?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?

If so, how much and from whom?
3.

What Order or Award?
7.
In order to substantiate the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to P12.
He also examined a doctor as PW.2 and got marked documents as per Ex.P.13 and 14 and closed his side evidence.

PW.1 and 2 tendered for cross examination done at length by the learned advocate for respondent No.2.
8.
On the other hand, to rebut the evidence of petitioner respondent No.2 has not adduced any oral or documentary evidence.
9. The documents got marked through PW.1 and 2

are - The true copy of FIR at Ex.P.1, true copy of complaint at Ex.P.2, true copy of spot mahazar at Ex.P.3, true copy of vehicle seizure mahazar, true copy of spot sketch at Ex.P.5, true copy of wound certificate at Ex.P.6, true copy of charge sheet at Ex.P.7, Xray report at Ex.P.8, Notarised copy of Aadhar card of PW1 at Ex.P.9, Medical bills at Ex.P.10, Xrays at Ex.P.11, CT scan at Ex.P.12, Clinical notes at Ex.P.13 and Xray at Ex.P.14.

10 . Having heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioner and the learned Counsel for the Respondent No.2, upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:

sentences.text: Issue No. 1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic accident that occurred on 31082018 at about 7.00 a.m. due to the rash and negligent driving of the tractor and trailer bearing Regn.No.KA40T9699 & KA03T1376 by its driver.
12. On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 has denied the involvement of said tractor and trailer in the alleged accident.
13. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, he got examined himself as P.W.1 and he also examined doctor as PW.2 and got marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P14 as noted above.
14. P.W.1 has reiterated the Petition averments in his chiefaffidavit.
He places reliance of the documents which are got marked as Ex. P.1 to 7 to substantiate the fact of involvement of vehicle in the alleged accident.

Upon careful consideration of the document, Ex.P2 i.e., the True copy of First information provided by one Mr.Shivakumar S/o Bheemanna, the recitals of the same discloses that on the fatal day, alleged accident occurred as a result of rash and negligence on the part of driver of tractor bearing No.KA08T 6289.

It is needless to mention that based on the said first information, the SHO of Malur police station registered a case in Cr.No.265/2018 against the driver of the tractor bearing Reg.No.KA08T6289 for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 337 and 304A of IPC.
15.

The recitals of document Ex.P.3 discloses that IO concerned having taken up investigation said to have drawn the spot mahazar on 01092018 between 3.00 to 3.45 p.m. in the presence of panchas mentioned therein.
The recitals of document Ex. P.3 clearly discloses the allegations made against the tractor bearing Regn.No.KA08T6289.
The recitals of Ex.P.4 discloses the fact that the said mahazar appears to have drawn on 09102018 in the presence of panchas mentioned therein.

The recitals of Ex. P.4 do not corroborate with the recitals of Ex. P.1 to 3 for the reason that,
Ex.P.4 discloses the number of vehicle bearing Regn.No.KA40T9699.
It is pertinent to note that the spot sketch Ex.P.5 is silent regarding nonmentioning of the registration number of the alleged vehicle said to have caused accident.
Whereas, Ex.P.5 only discloses regarding the registration number of the vehicle in which according to the petitioner he was proceeding as a pillion rider on the fatal day.

In this context, even Ex.P.5 do not corroborate to the contents of Ex. P.1 to 3.
16.

The careful consideration of other document i.e., Ex.P.7 makes it clear that the IO concerned said to have filed charge sheet against the alleged driver of vehicle bearing Regn.No.KA40T9699 and trailer bearing No.KA03T1376.
This Tribunal is conscious of the fact that the gravity of proof under the motor vehicles accident claim petitions is not as required under any other criminal proceedings.
However, law expects that the claimants/petitioners must probabilise their petition with the aid of oral and documentary evidence.

17. Keeping in mind the observations made in the above paragraphs careful consideration is to be given to the averments made in the petition as well as contentions raised by the respondent No.2 in it's statement of objections also keeping in mind the fact that inspite of valid service of notice upon the respondent No.1, he has remained absent.

This fact clearly establishes that the owner of the alleged tractor and trailer bearing Regn.No.KA40T9699 and KA03T1376 appears to have Jagannatha H.R vs M.Lakshman on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179668796/
4 falsely foisted the said vehicle in the petition hand in glove with the police authorities and also the petitioner herein in order to get compensation from the Tribunal.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India and the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka have held that whenever the materials which are brought before the Tribunal appears suspicious that in order to get compensation the vehicle which has valid insurance has been falsely implicated in the case, such petitions deserves to be dismissed.

19. In the entire case papers, there are no materials forthcoming to justify the fact as to how and on what basis does the IO arrived at a conclusion regarding the alleged involvement of KA40T9699 and KA03T1376 vehicle in the alleged accident.
Such aspect justify the contentions raised by the respondent No.2 regarding noninvolvement of said vehicle in the alleged accident.

20. It is also pertinent to note that during his cross examination, PW.1 has given clear admission of the fact that the first information discloses allegations against the vehicle bearing registration No.KA08T6289.

Such judicial admission coupled with the recitals of Ex.P.1 to 3 brings suspicion in the mind of this Tribunal regarding the case of petitioner in respect of alleged involvement of KA40T9699 and KA03T1376 and such suspicion supports the contention raised by the respondent No.2.

Apart from that, these observations lead this Tribunal to arrive at a conclusion that the petitioner has failed to probablise his case and that the case of the petitioner do not inspire confidence of this Tribunal.

21. In the backdrop of the observations made above, if the evidence given by PW.2 coupled with the documentary evidence Ex. P.6 and 8 are given careful consideration of, it is clear that though the petitioner said to have taken treatment initially at Malur hospital and R.L.Jalappa hospital, no such supportive documents are admittedly brought before this Tribunal.
The documents Ex.P.6 and 8 appears to have been secured belatedly for the purpose of this petition and they appears suspicious.

5

It is needless to mention that had the petitioner sustained any such injuries/fracture as a result of alleged accident, petitioner would not have waited for such a long duration without getting treated the same.

Such being the case, the Tribunal is of the opinion that the injuries which appear in Ex.
P.6 and 8 may not have caused as a result of alleged accident.
Moreover, there is an admission from PW.1 of the fact that he has not taken any treatment as an inpatient and that after the lapse of 19 days he admits to have obtained Ex.P.8 document.

All these factors justify the contentions raised by the respondent No.2.
22.

In addition to the above observations, if careful consideration is given to the oral evidence given by PW.2 and the documents Ex. P.13 and 14, this Tribunal is of the view that the evidence given by PW.2 will not come to the aid of petitioner as same do not support the petition averments.

Hence,
issue No.1 is answered in the 'Negative'.
23. Issue No. 2 : This Tribunal made observations in the above paragraphs that the petitioner has failed to probablise his case that he sustained grievous injuries as a result of accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of tractor and trailer bearing No. KA40T9699 and KA03T 1376.

As the petitioner has failed to prove the alleged involvement of tractor and trailer bearing No.
KA40T9699 and KA03T1376 in the accident in question, such being the situation of the case on hand, the petitioner is certainly not entitled for compensation.

Hence, issue No.2 is answered in the 'Negative'.
24. ISSUE No

. 3 : In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2 as above, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is hereby dismissed.
Draw Award accordingly.
